summary.name: WebStorm
summary.one_liner: WebStorm is JetBrains' JavaScript and TypeScript IDE that lets you prompt AI agents or write code yourself, with code intelligence used to verify changes.
use_cases: Delegating coding tasks to an AI agent inside the IDE
Migrating components from JavaScript to TypeScript
Refactoring and renaming symbols across a JS/TS project
Debugging and testing JavaScript or TypeScript code
Implementing UI components from a design source
summary.what_it_does: WebStorm is a JavaScript and TypeScript IDE with built-in AI agent support. You can type or dictate a task, or select code and send it to an agent, and choose agents from a built-in catalog or ones already installed locally. An Agent Sessions window tracks running and completed agent work, and diffs can be commented on and sent back as instructions. The IDE resolves usages, dependencies, and types across the codebase so agents can search, refactor, and migrate code using the IDE's code model rather than plain text matching. Editing, navigation, refactoring, testing, debugging, and Git commit history are available in the same window, and frameworks such as React, Angular, Vue, Next.js, TypeScript, and Node.js are preconfigured.
notable: Agent Sessions window for running multiple agents on one or several projects
Agents can open the browser, check console logs and network requests, and take screenshots to verify UI fixes
Built-in React, Angular, Vue, Next.js, TypeScript and Node.js support without extra plugins
caveats: Free for non-commercial use only; commercial use has a 30-day free trial
Agents can run on your own API key, a subscription you already pay for, or JetBrains AI, which is a paid option
One testimonial notes WebStorm uses more resources than VS Code
